cards.front: The two workloads in ride matching
cards.back: A firehose of driver location updates, and a much smaller stream of ride requests that each need a fast, one-driver-only decision.

cards.front: Location writes for 5M drivers pinging every 4 s
cards.back: About 1.25M a second, around 125 MB/s. This is the biggest load in the system.

cards.front: Size of the live driver index
cards.back: Only the latest point per driver: 5M × about 100 B is about 500 MB. It fits in memory on a handful of machines.

cards.front: Why a quote locks the price
cards.back: So the rider pays what they saw even if surge changes before pickup. Ride creation is also idempotent because riders double-tap.
Geohash is simple but cells distort and edge neighbours differ in prefix; quadtrees adapt to density but rebalance awkwardly; H3 hexagons have equidistant neighbours and cheap rings.

cards.front: Cells searched in k rings of H3
cards.back: 1 + 3k(k+1): 1, 7, 19, 37 for k = 0 to 3. Widen k until there are enough candidates.

cards.front: How the index handles a ping
cards.back: Compute the H3 cell. Same cell: update the record. New cell: remove from the old set and add to the new one, two in-memory operations.

cards.front: Why lossy location pings are fine
cards.back: Only the newest point matters and another arrives in 4 s, so pings aren't queued, retried or persisted synchronously.
A guarded compare-and-set moves the driver from available to offered with a 15 s expiry. Only one dispatcher's update can succeed.
Greedy matches each request at once; batched collects requests for 1-2 s per area and minimises total pickup time, giving better ETAs at busy times.

cards.front: How ETAs are fast enough for 50,000 a second
cards.back: Precomputed road graphs (contraction hierarchies) answer point-to-point in about 1 ms, with live traffic as edge weights and an ML correction.

cards.front: Why switchback tests for dispatch changes?
cards.back: Riders and drivers in one city affect each other, so the algorithm alternates by time window instead of splitting users into A and B.

quiz.q: Two dispatchers pick the same driver for two riders at the same moment. What makes sure only one wins?
choices: A guarded update from available to offered that succeeds for only one
Ranking by straight-line distance
Kafka ordering on the driver ID
Batched matching
quiz.why: The compare-and-set on the driver's state turns the race into a failed update and the next candidate.

quiz.q: Dispatch offers the closest driver by distance, but the pickup takes 15 minutes. Why?
choices: The H3 resolution is too fine
The driver is across a river; candidates should be ranked by road ETA
The ping rate is too low
Surge was capped
quiz.why: Straight-line distance ignores the road network.

quiz.q: A stadium empties and one city shard's request queue grows. Which mitigation fits?
choices: Persist every ping synchronously
Raise the offer expiry to 60 s
Split the hot region and switch to batched matching
Merge neighbouring cities into one shard
quiz.why: Hot regions are split further and batching improves overall matches at peak.

quiz.q: A location node holding a city shard dies. What is the impact?
choices: All trips in that city are lost
Drivers are double-booked
Surge pricing freezes
A few seconds of thinner search results while a replica or fresh node refills from pings
quiz.why: The live index is rebuildable from the ping stream within one interval.

quiz.q: A driver accepts an offer 20 seconds after it was sent. What happens?
choices: The guarded update fails and they see 'this ride is no longer available'
The rider gets two drivers
The accept is queued until the next ride
The trip service overrides the expiry
quiz.why: The offer expired at 15 s, so the accept no longer matches the expected state.

quiz.q: A rider's quote showed 1.3× surge, but surge rose to 1.8× before the driver arrived. What do they pay?
choices: 1.8×, the current surge
The average of the two
1.3×, captured in the quote
Base price with no surge
quiz.why: The quote captures the multiplier at request time.

quiz.q: Searching 3 rings at resolution 9 returns only 2 candidate drivers in a suburb. What should dispatch do?
choices: Offer to both at once
Widen the search with more rings
Return no drivers available
Switch the whole city to resolution 7
quiz.why: Dispatch widens k adaptively until there are enough candidates.
